sources.name: Lingo Lessons (Open Apps Studio)
sources.kind: code + course content + pre-generated TTS audio
sources.attribution: Based on Lingo Lessons by Open Apps Studio, used under the MIT License. The original LICENSE (including the 650 Industries, Inc. notice from the create-expo-app template) is preserved in this repository.
sources.notes: The base repository this fork continues. Bundled course packs and audio ship under the repository's MIT grant; the original audio generator and its TTS source were never published, so per-asset audio provenance is recorded as presumed rather than proven. A provenance audit of shipped assets remains a recorded obligation before any commercial distribution (approved plan, section I3.5). No new third-party dataset was ingested in Phase 2.

sources.name: Learning French with Tracy — authored French lexicon
sources.kind: authored lexical data (glosses reuse the project's existing course content)
sources.attribution: French lexicon data authored by the Learning French with Tracy project, published under CC BY-SA 4.0 (see LEXICON_LICENSE.md).
sources.notes: Original project authorship: part of speech, gender, topics, example sentences, and confusable relations for the 126 curriculum lexemes (content/fr/lexicon/lexemes.json, as of 2026-10-14); native glosses reuse the course content already covered by upstream-lingo-lessons. Lexique 4 has been retrieved (pinned by sha256 in content/fr/lexicon/source-manifest.json; see content/fr/lexicon/ACQUISITION.md): 123 of the 126 lexemes carry Lexique-4-derived frequency and IPA fields, each marked by a lexique-4 sourceRef and covered by the separate lexique-4 registry entry; the remaining 3 have project-authored IPA only. Published under CC BY-SA 4.0 per the approved licensing decision so the Lexique-4-derived data (also CC BY-SA 4.0) merges license-coherently. The dataset license never applies to application code, which keeps its existing MIT licensing.

sources.name: Lexique 4 (New, Pallier, Schalchli, Bourgin & Gimenes)
sources.kind: lexical database (frequency, contextual diversity, prevalence, phonology incl. IPA, lemmas, verb morphology)
sources.attribution: Word frequency, prevalence and IPA pronunciation data from Lexique 4: New, B., Pallier, C., Schalchli, G., Bourgin, J., & Gimenes, M. (2026). Lexique 4: A major upgrade of the Lexique French lexical database. Behavior Research Methods. Distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://lexique.org).
sources.notes: Official artifact Lexique400.tsv pinned by sha256 in content/fr/lexicon/source-manifest.json (33,067,258 bytes, 189,863 rows, retrieved from https://lexique.org/databases/Lexique400/Lexique400.tsv by the dispatch-only acquisition workflow; raw file never committed). Column mapping: content/fr/lexicon/LEXIQUE4_COLUMNS.md; cross-check dispositions: content/fr/lexicon/REVIEW.md pass 3. Imported fields per matched lexeme: frequency (12_FreqLemme raw + population rank + population-quantile band) and pronunciation (3_Phono_IPA verbatim, genuine IPA). CC BY-SA 4.0 share-alike is satisfied by the project's CC BY-SA 4.0 lexicon dataset licensing (LEXICON_LICENSE.md).

sources.name: Learning French with Tracy — authored French pedagogy
sources.kind: authored teaching content (concept explanations, rules, examples, guidebooks)
sources.attribution: French pedagogy content authored by the Learning French with Tracy project.
sources.notes: Clean-room authored teaching content for the Phase 5B pedagogy units (gender & articles, high-yield verbs, cognates & false friends, numbers, connected French). Linguistic FACTS are drawn from the referenced sources recorded in content/fr/pedagogy/RESEARCH.md (institutional references such as Académie française and OQLF usage pages, plus this repository's Lexique-4-derived population statistics); all PROSE is original. Statistical claims in concepts additionally carry a lexique-4 sourceRef. Ships under the repository's MIT grant like the course packs (the CC BY-SA dataset boundary covers the lexicon only).

sources.name: ts-fsrs (open-spaced-repetition)
sources.kind: code (runtime scheduling library)
sources.attribution: Spaced-repetition scheduling powered by ts-fsrs, © open-spaced-repetition contributors, MIT License.
sources.notes: FSRS-6 scheduler. The SM-2 migration math is an independent TypeScript implementation of the published memory_state_from_sm2 formula from fsrs-rs (also MIT).

CC BY-SA 4.0 share-alike accepted deliberately: the project already publishes its derived French dataset under CC BY-SA 4.0 (approved plan, section AC2) and ships an in-app attributions screen, so the obligations are already implemented. The reception audio derived from this voice carries the same license and attribution.

sources.name: kaikki.org Wiktextract (English Wiktionary edition)
sources.kind: lexical data (per-language JSONL dumps)
sources.attribution: Lexical data (lemmas, parts of speech, inflected forms, gender, IPA, senses, example sentences) derived from Wiktionary via Wiktextract / kaikki.org (Tatu Ylonen), used under CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution to the Wiktionary contributors; kaikki.org and Ylonen (LREC 2022) are cited. The lexicon dataset is published under CC BY-SA 4.0 (LEXICON_LICENSE.md).
sources.notes: P3a lexicon ETL v2 primary lexical source. Each language's dump is pinned (sha256, bytes, date) in content/<lang>/lexicon/source-manifest.json by the dispatch-only workflow .github/workflows/lexicon-source.yml; raw dumps are never committed. Per-lexeme provenance is the `word|pos` key in sourceRefs; examples carry `word|pos|sense`.

sources.name: kaikki.org Wiktextract (Vietnamese Wiktionary edition)
sources.kind: lexical data (Vietnamese glosses and examples)
sources.attribution: Vietnamese glosses and example translations derived from the Vietnamese Wiktionary via Wiktextract / kaikki.org, used under CC BY-SA 4.0 with attribution to the Vietnamese Wiktionary contributors.
sources.notes: P3a: the primary source of `glosses.vi` / `translations.vi`. Entries that only redirect are skipped; a lexeme without a Vietnamese sense carries the draft marker TODO:vi until the authoring toolkit (P3c) fills it — the marker blocks compile for any -vi course.

sources.name: FrequencyWords (hermitdave) — OpenSubtitles 2018 word frequencies
sources.kind: word frequency lists
sources.attribution: Word frequencies derived from the FrequencyWords lists (OpenSubtitles 2018; content CC BY-SA 4.0, code MIT) by Hermit Dave. Modifications: lemmatisation through the kaikki form index, population ranking and quantile banding (content/<lang>/lexicon/derived/frequency-stats.json).
sources.notes: P3a primary frequency measurement (`frequency.source`). Per-million values are relative to the list total, not the corpus (documented in frequency-stats.json).

sources.name: wordfreq 3.1.1 (Robyn Speer) — Zipf word frequencies
sources.kind: word frequency data (exported Zipf values)
sources.attribution: Secondary frequency evidence from wordfreq (Speer, R. (2022). rspeer/wordfreq: v3.0 (v3.0.2). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7199437), data CC BY-SA 4.0 (incorporating Google Books Ngram and SUBTLEX components with their acknowledgements), code Apache-2.0.
sources.notes: P3a: `zipf` column of the candidate pools only (authoring evidence); never the `frequency` field of a lexeme.

sources.name: Tatoeba — sentences and translation links

sources.attribution: Example sentences from the Tatoeba Project (https://tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR; each sentence credits its contributor by username in content/<lang>/lexicon/derived/tatoeba-credits.json and carries its sentence ids in the example `key`.
sources.notes: P3a example fallback when a kaikki sense has no usable example. Audio is never used (per-contributor licences).
